blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park has a great variety of animals like the Big Five, and the chance that you will encounter lions climbing up trees is greater here than in other parks! Ruaha National Park is not only the second-largest park, but is probably home to more elephants than any other national park in East Africa. And Nyerere National Park (previously Selous Game Reserve) is not only Tanzania’s largest park, but also UNESCO World Heritage Site due to its wildlife diversity and undisturbed nature.
blocks.html: In Mikumi National Park you find a wide range of animals, including the Big Five, and you are more likely to see tree-climbing lions here than in other parks! Ruaha National Park is the second-largest park and probably holds more elephants than any other national park in East Africa. Nyerere National Park (formerly Selous Game Reserve) is the largest park in Tanzania and, thanks to its wildlife diversity and untouched nature, a UNESCO World Heritage Site as well.

blocks.orig: This private safari offers you the flexibility to travel at your own pace, exactly the way you like it. You will have a private safari vehicle and guide.
blocks.html: Because this safari is private, you are free to travel at your own pace and exactly as you wish. Both the safari vehicle and the guide are yours alone.

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: A question we hear a lot from travellers is when they should visit Tanzania. Honestly, no single answer is correct. It comes down to what you hope to see, where you would like to go, your interests and your budget. You can read our detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: With our safaris in Tanzania you get the chance to discover the country’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our speciality, so the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is reserved for you alone. You choose when each safari day begins and ends, and on the day itself our experienced guides are happy to help you decide. Perhaps you would like to see the animals at sunrise and sunset, when they are most active and the temperature is comfortable, or perhaps you prefer to finish the day at the pool; it’s entirely your call. Because Tanzania’s wildlife is active at different moments of the day, you’ll get many chances to watch the animals in action.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, definitely. Tanzania is known as one of the best places to see the Big Five. You can watch these impressive animals (lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo) in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, definitely. Tanzania is a welcoming and safe country to travel in. Especially in tourist areas such as Arusha, the atmosphere is hospitable, and you can enjoy the beautiful scenery and wildlife with peace of mind. The local people are friendly. As anywhere else in the world, it is always sensible to take basic precautions, like keeping an eye on your belongings. Tanzania’s natural beauty and warm-hearted people make it a wonderful country to visit.

blocks.orig: Welcome to Tanzania! Upon your arrival at Dar es Salaam Airport, our friendly and knowledgeable guide will be eagerly waiting to warmly welcome you. He will be readily available to assist you and ensure a smooth transfer to your hotel. Sit back, relax, and let us take care of all your travel needs, providing you with a memorable and unforgettable experience in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Welcome to Tanzania! When you land at Dar es Salaam Airport, our friendly guide, who knows the country well, is looking forward to giving you a warm welcome. He is there to help you and makes sure your transfer to the hotel goes smoothly. Lean back and relax while we look after everything you need during your travels, so your time in Tanzania becomes an experience to remember.

blocks.orig: Mikumi National Park lies at a six-hour drive from Dar Es Salaam and is Tanzania's fourth largest national park. The open horizons and abundant wildlife draw frequent comparisons to the more famous Serengeti plains, but its location close to Tanzania's largest city makes Mikumi easier accessible. The park has a great variety of animals: elephants, buffalos, zebras and giraffes are relatively easy to spot, as well as lions mating and many hippos in the resident hippo pool!
blocks.html: A six-hour drive from Dar Es Salaam brings you to Mikumi National Park, the fourth largest national park in Tanzania. Its wide horizons and plentiful wildlife are often compared with the better-known Serengeti plains, yet because it is near Tanzania's largest city, Mikumi is easier to reach. You will see a wide range of animals: elephants, buffalos, zebras and giraffes are fairly easy to find, and so are mating lions and the many hippos in the park's own hippo pool!

blocks.orig: Ruaha National Park is the third largest national park in Tanzania. It lies along the Great Ruaha River, is known for its large elephant population, and is a true paradise for birdwatchers with over 570 species. Besides, you might catch a glimpse of lions, leopards, giraffes, zebras, crocodiles, elands, sable antelopes, jackals, or the rare African wild dog. Game drives are special, as you drive through an untouched ecosystem in this relatively quiet but stunning park!
blocks.html: As Tanzania's third largest national park, Ruaha National Park stretches along the Great Ruaha River. It is famous for its big elephant population, and with more than 570 species it is a real paradise for birdwatchers. You may also spot lions, leopards, giraffes, zebras, crocodiles, elands, sable antelopes, jackals or the rare African wild dog. Game drives here feel special, because this fairly quiet yet beautiful park takes you through an untouched ecosystem!

blocks.orig: Today you discover the jungle, savannah and river sides of the vast Nyerere National Park (previously the Selous Game Reserve) - an amazing place for game drives. This park in southern Tanzania has fewer visitors than the northern parks but boasts elephants, hippos, crocodiles, lions, leopards, giraffes, the endangered rhino, the rare African wild dog and more. It's the second largest park in the country after Serengeti National Park, so be prepared to cover some miles!
blocks.html: Today you explore the jungle, the savannah and the riverbanks of the huge Nyerere National Park (formerly the Selous Game Reserve), a wonderful setting for game drives. This southern Tanzanian park receives fewer visitors than the parks in the north, yet it is home to elephants, hippos, crocodiles, lions, leopards, giraffes, the endangered rhino, the rare African wild dog and other animals. After Serengeti National Park it is the second largest park in the country, so expect to cover quite a few miles!

blocks.orig: A boat safari on the Rufiji River in Nyerere National Park is both relaxing and adventurous! The boat takes you over the river and to nearby lakes, allowing you to spot many animals that come to the water’s edge. Very common are giraffes, impalas, waterbucks, kudus and warthogs. Sometimes, also bathing elephants or crocodiles can be seen, and always, the many bird species sound their voices. The trip includes a picnic lunch on the shores of one of the lakes.
blocks.html: In Nyerere National Park, a boat safari on the Rufiji River is relaxing and adventurous at the same time! You sail along the river and on to lakes nearby, so you can watch the many animals that come down to the water. Giraffes, impalas, waterbucks, kudus and warthogs are seen very often. Now and then you may also see elephants bathing or crocodiles, and you always hear the calls of the many bird species. A picnic lunch on the shore of one of the lakes is part of the trip.

blocks.orig: This is your last day! Today you fly to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam, from where you will catch your international flight home. Having second thoughts? Then don't hesitate to extend your holiday to one of Tanzania's paradise islands such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia!
blocks.html: Your final day has arrived! Today you take a flight to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam, where you board your international flight home. Not ready to leave yet? Feel free to add a stay on one of Tanzania's paradise islands such as Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia to your holiday!
